{{Infobox Species |image= {{Media |defaultTypeTab= Model |Artwork TWW= [[File:TWW Koroks Artwork.png|320x320px]] |Artwork TWWHD= [[File:TWWHD Makar Artwork.png|320x320px]] |Artwork TotK= [[File:TotK Korok Artwork.png|320x320px]] |Model TWW= [[File:TWW Makar Model.png|320x320px]] |Model TWWHD= [[File:TWWHD Makar Model.png|320x320px]] |Model BotW= [[File:BotW Korok Model.png|320x320px]] |Model TotK= [[File:TotK Korok Model.png|320x320px]] }} |caption= |game= TWW, BotW, TotK |other= AoC, AoI |pronunciation= |plural= Koroks{{Cite Book|quote= |book= E |publisher= |page= 51}} |characteristics= {{List| * Tree-like bodies * Leaf masks }} |habitat= {{Infobox Game Blocks |TWW= [[Forest Haven]] |BotW= [[Korok Forest]] }} |attack= |weapon= |members= {{List| * [[Aldo]] * [[Drona]] * [[Elma]] * [[Hollo]] * [[Irch]] * [[Linder]] * [[Makar]] * [[Oakin]] * [[Olivio]] * [[Rown]] * [[Hestu]] * [[Chio]] * [[Walton]] * [[Kula]] * [[Damia]] * [[Maca]] }} }} The {{Term/Store|Korok|Koroks|Series, BotW|plural}} are a race in {{TLoZ Series}}.{{Cite|Korok|Game Screen|BotW}} They are small, wooden people who wear leaf masks over their faces. Their personalities may differ greatly, and are often reflected in their masks. They are spirits who are watched over by the [[Great Deku Tree]].{{Cite|Well, then, Link... These are the Koroks -- the spirits of the forest. [...] Now they fear people...but to me, they will ever be my cherished little children.|Great Deku Tree|TWW}} They are protectors of the forest they live in. In {{TWW}}, the Koroks are the transformed forms of the [[Kokiri]] following the [[Great Flood]].{{Cite|Once upon a time, long ago, the Koroks took on human forms, but when they came to live on the sea, they took these shapes.|Great Deku Tree|TWW}}{{Cite Book|quote= Aonuma: We created the Rito as the evolved form of the Zora that appeared in "Ocarina of Time" and the Koroks as what the Kokiri became once they left the forest. They appear different, but they have inherited their blood.|book= ''[[Zelda Box]]''|publisher= Enterbrain|page= 29}} ==Characteristics== The Koroks appear as little wooden people whose bodies resemble [[Tree]]s, and whose faces are concealed by leaf masks. The masks they wear take on various different shapes based on types of leaves, and have holes in them resembling eyes and a mouth, and occasionally a hole for their noses to fit through. Their bodies make a jingling sound whenever they move. Koroks are also able to fly through the use of propeller [[Deku Leaf|Deku Leaves]] that sprout from their bodies.{{Cite|We Koroks can fly through the sky using our own {{Color TWW|Red|Deku Leaves}}.|Korok|TWW}} The Koroks in {{TWW|-}} are watched over by the Great Deku Tree in the [[Forest Haven]]. According to him, the Koroks originally took on human forms as Kokiri before changing their shape following the Great Flood. The Koroks are very shy, and do not normally appear to humans.{{Cite|Koroks! Little children of the woods! This traveler is not your enemy. Let your hearts be at ease, and show yourselves!|Great Deku Tree|TWW}} ===Korok Ceremony=== The '''Korok Ceremony''' is an important event for the Koroks and Great Deku Tree in {{TWW|-}}.{{Cite|Even after the Korok ceremony, Hollo remains in the Forest Haven researching potion-making.|Figurine|TWW}} Once a year,{{Cite|As it happens, you have come just in time for a ceremony that the Koroks hold but once every year. It is about to begin.|Great Deku Tree|TWW}} the Great Deku Tree sprouts [[Forest Tree]] seeds which are then taken by the Koroks to plant throughout the [[Great Sea]] and watch over their growth, in the hopes that new forests will grow and more land will cover the Sea.{{Cite|Every year after the Koroks perform this ceremony, they fly off to the distant islands on the sea and plant my seeds in the hopes that new forests will grow.|Great Deku Tree|TWW}} It is the Great Deku Tree's hope that the islands will join as one land by planting these forests.{{Cite|Forests hold great power: they can change one tiny island into a much larger island. Soon, a day will come when all the islands are one, connected by earth and grove. And the people who live on that great island will be able to join hands and, together, create a better world. Such is my dream.|Great Deku Tree|TWW}} A mysterious power dwells within the seeds, and they must all be planted simultaneously or they will wither.{{Cite Book|quote= A mysterious power dwells within the Great Deku's seeds created during their annual ceremnony, and they must all be planted simultaneously or they will wither.|book= E |publisher= |page= 51}} The Ceremony can only commence once the Korok [[Makar]] has played his [[Violin]] for the Great Deku Tree.{{Cite|Makar is in charge of the musical performance at the ceremony held each year by the Koroks in the Forest Haven.|Figurine|TWW}} ==History== ==={{TWW|-}}=== In {{TWW}}, the Kokiri had transformed into the Koroks following the [[Great Flood]]. They continue to live with the Great Deku Tree, on an island called the [[Forest Haven]]. Once every year, the Koroks hold the annual Korok Ceremony so that the Great Deku Tree can produce seeds that can be planted throughout the [[Great Sea]], with the hope and dream of uniting the islands into one vast land by growing forests. A Korok named [[Makar]] plays his Violin so the Great Deku Tree can produce his seeds. It appears, however, that the Great Deku Tree's and Koroks' efforts have been unsuccessful over the years as they do not seem to have made much progress. Link encounters the Koroks after saving the Great Deku Tree from a swarm of [[ChuChu]]s. By his reassurance, the Koroks emerge from their hiding to meet Link. The Great Deku Tree welcomes Link to the Ceremony they are about to hold, but is interrupted when [[Linder]] arrives in a panic saying that Makar had fallen into the [[Forbidden Forest]].{{Cite|N-No! It is not that, O Great Deku Tree! Makar...fell into the {{Color TWW|Red|Forbidden Woods}}!|Linder|TWW}} The Great Deku asks Link to go into the Forest to rescue Makar, giving him a [[Deku Leaf]] so he may reach the place. After Link finds and rescues Makar from [[Kalle Demos]], they return to the Forest Haven where the Koroks commence the annual Korok Ceremony. The Great Deku Tree produces several seeds that eight of the Koroks take and leave to plant throughout the Great Sea. Makar and [[Hollo]], a Korok [[Potion]]-maker, stay behind in the Forest Haven. Link can find the other Koroks in several isles across the Great Sea, having planted their seeds in their respective islands. Each of them, however, are in despair that the sprouts they have planted are withering, and will not be able to grow into forests.{{Cite|I've come here to plant the Great Deku Tree's seed... But look! Usually, the forest trees sprout quite vigorously wherever you plant them, but for some reason, this one has withered... ...I'd be willing to bet that the trees my fellow Koroks have planted are withering, as well. It seems that when one tree fails to grow from its seed, {{Color TWW|Red|all}} the {{Color TWW|Red|forest trees}} from that year's seeds {{Color TWW|Red|wither}} and {{Color TWW|Red|fail}} to grow tall and mighty.|Korok|TWW}} They ask that Link bring back some [[Forest Water]] from the Forest Haven and sprinkle it onto the trees so they may be revived.{{Cite|Maybe if we could sprinkle the {{Color TWW|Red|water}} from the {{Color TWW|Red|Forest Haven}} on the tree... Maybe then this sapling would be saved.|Korok|TWW}} If Link manages to water every sprout before the Forest Water loses its potency, the Forest Trees will grow healthy and the Great Deku Tree's dream will finally be realized. Later during his quest, Link encounters the spirit of [[Fado (The Wind Waker)|Fado]], the deceased Kokiri [[Sage|Sage of Wind]]. Fado was killed by [[Ganondorf]]'s forces, causing the [[Master Sword]] to lose its power. Fado requests that Link finds the one destined to become the next Sage of Wind, who carries the same Violin as he.{{Cite|You wish to return the power to your blade, don't you? In that case, look for the {{Color TWW|Red|one}} who has the same {{Color TWW|Red|instrument}} that I hold, and teach him the {{Color TWW|Red|song}} you just played. Once you do, I'm certain the holder of the instrument will feel the blood of the sages awaken within his veins.|Fado (The Wind Waker)|TWW}} Link locates Makar and, after playing the "[[Wind God's Aria]]", awakens him as the new Sage of Wind. Together they travel to the [[Wind Temple]] where after Link defeats its evil, Makar prays so that the Master Sword regains some of its power. ==={{BotW|-}}=== In {{BotW}}, Koroks can be found all over [[Hyrule]] hidden throughout the land.{{Cite|Oh, and my friends are hiding in lots of different places too! Don't be shy about poking your nose into suspicious places!|Korok|BotW}} Link must solve a wide array of puzzles in order to make a Korok appear.{{Cite|Ya-ha-ha! You found me!|Korok|BotW}} The first time Link finds a Korok, it will be surprised that Link can see him.{{Cite|Huh? You're not Hestu! But you can...see me? I didn't know your kind could see the children of the forest!|Korok|BotW}} Their arrival is followed by the gift of a [[Korok Seed]], which can then be traded to [[Hestu]],{{Cite|Well, if you run into Hestu, please return this to him.|Korok|BotW}} a very large Korok first encountered on the path to [[Kakariko Village]]. Trading Korok Seeds expands Link's equipment slots, allowing him to carry more weapons, shields and bows. The price of expansion increases after every trade. After a few trades, Hestu will strike out for his home in [[Korok Forest]]. He can be encountered one final time at the [[Woodland Stable]], [[Riverside Stable]], or [[Wetland Stable]], where one can upgrade Link's [[Inventory]] again. After a few more trades, Hestu will once again go on his way back home. Koroks are by far the most varied race in this game, with over 913 different Koroks overall. This includes the 900 hidden Koroks, the 13 NPCs, all of whom can be found in or around the Korok forest at some point, and other Koroks in the forest who hide when Link approaches; these last ones can't be interacted with and are purely cosmetic, but they show just how many exist. In the center of the [[Lost Woods]], the [[Great Deku Tree]] resides over the Korok Forest, the home of the Koroks. Many Koroks can be found here, though most will hide when Link gets close. A few, such as [[Chio]], will converse with Link. After collecting all 900 Korok Seeds, Hestu will tell Link that all the Koroks have returned to the Korok Forest,{{Cite|{{Big|Hey! Guess what!}} All of the forest children returned to the Korok Forest! You must have had an army of people searching for them, huh?|Hestu|BotW}} though the Koroks can still be found in their original locations. It is stated that most people cannot see Koroks, which is why some are confused as to how Link can see them. It is implied though that Link is not the only one, as the [[Hateno Village|Hateno-born]] merchant [[Agus]] says he was spooked by a big tree ghost by [[Lake Siela]]; this is where the oversized Korok [[Hestu]] can originally be found, meaning that is likely what Agus saw. He didn't interact with the "tree ghost" though, meaning Link was the first; this caused Hestu to be taken aback when Link talks to him as he did not expect it. ==={{TotK|-}}=== In {{TotK}}, Koroks can be found throughout [[Hyrule]], similarly as in {{BotW}}, and are located throughout the [[Surface]] and the [[Sky]]. Upon completing various small puzzles, [[Link]] will receive a [[Korok Seed]] from them, which he can then bring to [[Hestu]], who can increase his [[Inventory]] space in exchange for the seeds. Some Koroks can be found traveling with another fellow Korok, but unable to move and struggling to keep up with them, requiring that Link use his various abilities in order to reunite the Korok with its partner, which will earn him two Korok Seeds. ====Members==== {{Gallery List|Characters |TotK= Chio, Damia, Daz, Great Deku Tree, Hestu, Jatora, Kula, Maca, Maheli, Mopu, Mokka, Nako, Natie, Oaki, Pepp, Raha, Walton }} ==Other Appearances== ==={{AoC|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} In {{AoC}}, Koroks are hidden in various locations in the Story Missions, just like in {{BotW}}. They usually take the shape of a pinwheel, but can appear as [[Leaves with Fairy Dust]] and [[Race (Mechanic)|Races]] as well. These can simply be interacted with using the Y button to reveal the Korok, which will then give a Korok Seed. Balloons may also hide some Koroks, some of which cannot be hit with attacks normally and require the player to use [[Stasis]] before popping the balloon. Hestu can summon Koroks as part of his attacks. These summoned Koroks will contribute to most of his attacks, including through use of [[Rune|Sheikah Runes]]. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoI|-}}=== {{Stub|AoI}} ==Trivia== * Being plant-based creatures, Koroks fear vegetarians.{{Cite|Zzz... No. Vegetarians everywhere! STOP! THAT'S MY FACE!
Ahhh! Sorry about that. I must have dozed off for a bit...|Pepp|BotW}} ==Nomenclature== The Koroks in {{TWW|-}} are named after types of trees. The name "Korok" is derived from {{Wp|Koropokkuru}}, little creatures that hide in Butterbur plants in Ainu folklore.{{Fact|TWWHD}} {{Nomenclature}} ==Gallery== {{All Images}} File:TWW Korok Group Artwork.png|{{Game Label|{{TWW|-}}}}Artwork of Koroks File:TWW Makar Artwork.png|{{Game Label|{{TWW|-}}}}Artwork of Makar, a Korok File:Newyear.jpg|{{Game Label|{{TWW|-}}}}Koroks singing during the Korok Ceremony File:BotW Koroks.png|{{Game Label|{{BotW|-}}}}A cluster of Koroks File:BotW Korok Concept Artwork.png|{{Game Label|{{BotW|-}}}}Korok concept art File:BotW Leaves with Fairy Dust Model.png|{{Game Label|{{BotW|-}}}}The visual effect that marks the location of certain hidden Koroks File:TotK Korok Model 2.png|{{Game Label|{{TotK|-}}}}A Korok with a backpack File:TotK Korok Promotional Screenshot.png|{{Game Label|{{TotK|-}}}}A promotional screenshot of a Korok File:AoC Korok Model.png|{{Game Label|{{AoC|-}}}}A Korok File:AoC Korok Promotional Screenshot.png|{{Game Label|{{AoC|-}}}}A promotional screenshot of a Korok File:AoC Korok Promotional Screenshot 2.png|{{Game Label|{{AoC|-}}}}A promotional screenshot of a Korok File:BotW Japan Expo Thank You Artwork.png|{{Game Label|{{Series|Display}}}}Artwork thanking attendees of The Art of {{Series|Display}} Masterclass featuring Koroks File:Nintendo TOKYO TLoZ Korok Promotional Artwork.jpg|{{Game Label|}}Promotional artwork for "{{TLoZ|-}} Korok" merchandise series from Nintendo TOKYO featuring Koroks {{Ref| {{Cite|{{Color AoI|Gray|People}}
